method: Searched each repo's PRs, issues and commits with the GitHub search API (OR-grouped phrases for cycle terms, TDZ/undefined-import error strings, barrel/re-export terms, load-order terms; title-restricted searches for the large repos; 116 searches in total, each logged with its hit count). Plausible hits were read with gh pr view / gh pr diff / gh api commits; only merged fixes were kept. For each, the fix commit's first parent (or the PR base when the PR merged without a merge commit) was fetched with gh api contents, the import lines of every file on the cycle were read and quoted with line numbers, and the use of the imported binding was classified as module-evaluation (class extends, top-level call or object literal) or function-internal. Cycles through virtual modules were traced through the code-generation strings that produce them. Nothing from the repos was installed, built or run.

bugs.title: fix(v4): break circular import between classic schemas and iso (#5275)
bugs.symptom: Issue #5362 (zod 4.1.12, webpack with a cycle checker): "ERROR in Detected 2 cycles which exceeds configured limit of 0 / ERROR in node_modules/zod/v4/classic/iso.js -> node_modules/zod/v4/classic/schemas.js -> node_modules/zod/v4/classic/iso.js". Issue #6073 (Rollup): "(!) Circular dependency node_modules/zod/v4/classic/schemas.js -> node_modules/zod/v4/classic/iso.js -> node_modules/zod/v4/classic/schemas.js". Issue #5275: "This caused issues in our build stack".
bugs.runtimeImpact: build failure for consumers with a strict cycle checker; bundler warnings; no runtime crash reported
bugs.fixShape: moved code to new module: the ZodISO* classes moved into schemas.ts; iso.ts became a one-way facade that re-exports them
bugs.notes: Both directions are used only lazily: iso.ts calls schemas.ZodStringFormat.init(inst, def) inside the core.$constructor initializer (iso.ts:19), which runs at instance construction, and schemas.ts calls iso.datetime() etc. inside method closures (schemas.ts:562-565). So the cycle never failed at runtime; it failed builds. The PR added a static no-circular-imports test for v4/classic and a Rollup-based test.

bugs.title: 4.2.1 (fix for #5536: from-json-schema.ts imported the ../index.js barrel)
bugs.symptom: "TypeError: Cannot read property 'fromJSONSchema' of undefined" — "Getting this error when using `zod` with react native/expo. Issue only occurs on zod@4.2.0, zod@4.1.13 works fine." Maintainer: "Fixed in 4.2.1" linking this commit.
bugs.runtimeImpact: crash at import time under React Native / Metro; the release that introduced from-json-schema.ts (4.2.0) broke Expo apps
bugs.fixShape: replaced barrel import with direct imports: a local `const z = { ..._schemas, ..._checks, iso: _iso }` built from ./schemas.js, ./checks.js and ./iso.js (plus a madge check:circular CI job)
bugs.notes: The package entry packages/zod/src/index.ts imports ./v4/classic/external.js, so loading zod enters external.ts, which reaches from-json-schema.ts, which imports the v4 barrel that re-exports external.ts again. In the TypeScript source `z` is only used inside function bodies (e.g. from-json-schema.ts:66 `return z.never();`), so the failure needs a module system that reads the barrel's bindings eagerly; per the issue it showed up under Metro/React Native only. Extra edges: v4/index.ts:1 `import z4 from "./classic/index.js";` and classic/index.ts:1 `import * as z from "./external.js";`. PR #5537 proposed the same fix and was closed unmerged.

A longer cycle at the base has a top-level use: src/types/any.ts:10 `export class ZodAny extends z.ZodType<any, ZodAnyDef> {` (z = ./base), base.ts:11 imports ../parser, parser.ts:3 imports ./index, which imports ./types/any. bugs.title: refactor: break circular dependencies to fix test-unit
bugs.symptom: "Some circular dependency in the code base was making the tests fail locally. This PR removes the circular dependencies to fix it." Commit 5300f2f: "breaks the following circular dependecy: config.ts -> server/environments/runnableEnvironment.ts -> server/environment.ts -> config.ts". Commit f25a8de lists a 9-module cycle (server/environment.ts -> plugins/optimizedDeps.ts -> optimizer/index.ts -> optimizer/esbuildDepPlugin.ts -> plugins/css.ts -> build.ts -> config.ts -> server/environments/runnableEnvironment.ts -> server/environment.ts).
bugs.runtimeImpact: unit tests failed locally (error text not quoted); no user-facing report
bugs.topLevelUse: packages/vite/src/node/server/environments/runnableEnvironment.ts:34 `class RunnableDevEnvironment extends DevEnvironment {` — class extends at module evaluation. If server/environment.ts is entered first, it imports ../config (line 11) before declaring DevEnvironment (line 45), config.ts imports runnableEnvironment.ts, and the extends clause reads DevEnvironment in its TDZ.
bugs.fixShape: moved code: getDefaultResolvedEnvironmentOptions moved out of config.ts (to server/environment.ts, then baseEnvironment.ts); ERR_* constants moved from plugins/optimizedDeps.ts to constants.ts
bugs.notes: config.ts:41 also imports `{ DevEnvironment } from './server/environment'`, so config.ts <-> server/environment.ts is itself a 2-cycle (value edges both ways). The PR does not quote the failing error, so `kind` stays circular-fix; the top-level extends is the only module-evaluation use I found on the cycle. Vite ships a bundle, so source-level cycles only bite when the source runs unbundled (vitest, tsx); see notes.vite for a live one.

bugs.notes: VS Code uses relative specifiers here, so no tsconfig path alias is involved. The PR background: "historically we have never allowed to have cyclic runtime dependencies between our modules. The AMD loader would simply fail during load. Since the advent of ESM this has changed, browsers handle cycling dependencies graceful and things might work or not - it depends on the circumstances in which things get loaded ... we have added a check for cyclic runtime dependencies (as part of the ESM work). Unfortunately, this check was broken and a couple of cyclic dependencies have slipped in." The PR lists 12 cycles its checker found (chat, editor tokens, GPU raster, tree-sitter, notebook, SCM, extensions, prompt-syntax parsers). I verified the notebook cycle reaches the throwing file; I did not reproduce which entry order the test hit, and connor4312 also landed MCP cycle fixes in the same PR.

notes.zod: 4 confirmed (2020-21 restructure for the ESM build, 2022, 2025 Metro crash, 2026 bundler-checker failures). Zod now runs madge --circular in CI (since 4.2.1, excluding v4/core, v3 and iso.ts) and a static no-circular-imports test for v4/classic (since #5926). Two of the four involve the package's own entry barrels.
notes.hono: 3 confirmed, all reported as bundler warnings (Rollup, Expo/Metro), none crashed. Two of three were fixed by importing from the defining module instead of an index file.
notes.trpc: 2 cycles in 1 PR (#3877), Rollup warnings during their own build; no runtime symptom. No other own-source cycle fixes found; cycle-related issues are user-land.
notes.excalidraw: 3 confirmed cross-package cycles through the @excalidraw/* package barrels (tsconfig paths); one crashed the browser example via a top-level read (10544). Perf: two PRs (7635, 7640) removed re-exports from internal index.ts barrels to keep react-dom/react/jotai out of @excalidraw/utils.
notes.vite: 1 own-source fix (18237). Most cycle work in Vite is tool-level (HMR/SSR handling of user cycles; 18 entries in toolHandlesCycles). A live cycle with a top-level read sits in the corpus snapshot: node/config.ts <-> node/server/index.ts (config.ts:897 `server: serverConfigDefaults,`); issue #22634 hit it as a TDZ when running the source with tsx and was closed as unsupported, because the published bundle orders the modules safely. Perf searches found lazy-import fixes (20646 "dynamically import resolveConfig", 15621 "lazy load rollup during dev", 6898) but no barrel removals.
notes.astro: 2 confirmed in packages/astro/src, both through virtual modules that act as barrels (astro/app entry, astro:assets); a file-based graph cannot see them. One more (16968, Cloudflare adapter) needs the user's file to close the cycle (unverified). 5 tool-level entries.
notes.nextjs: No confirmed own-source cycle bug. Title/body searches for circular/cycle/cyclic/TDZ in merged PRs return Turbopack (Rust) bundler fixes and comment noise; the one packages/next title hit (68858) has no static cycle at its parent. Next.js's barrel work is a tool feature for user dependencies: #54572 (2023-08-25) added the `optimize_barrel` SWC transform and `optimizePackageImports` (no numbers in the PR). Import-cost fixes in its own source are lazy requires rather than barrel removals: #41354 "it's an extra ~15ms win on cold boots (tested locally) and we are now at around 68ms (started from 110+)"; #77723 "decreases the dev runtime bundle size for both Webpack and Turbopack by **16%**, and it decreases the prod runtime bundle size for Turbopack by **12%**" (splitting runtime bundles per bundler); #91387 stops requiring watchpack in production.
notes.vscode: 3 confirmed. VS Code treats module cycles as a build error: under AMD "The AMD loader would simply fail during load"; after the ESM migration a compile-time check landed (#235808, 2024-12-11), was found broken, and #251003 (2025-06-11) fixed 12 cycles at once, one of which caused a TDZ (#250990). A standalone script and tests followed (#296035, 2026-02-18). Many "cyclic dependency" hits are dependency-injection service cycles or observable cycles, not module cycles (rejected).
notes.search: GitHub search strips punctuation, so "export *" and "index file" match almost everything; those two terms were dropped after the first batch (the zod/hono runs that used them are kept in `searched` with their noisy counts). Commit search only indexes default branches. For the four large repos PR searches were limited to is:merged. 114 issue/PR/commit searches plus 2 code searches.
